{"metadata":{"description":"DSH 嵌入式硬件沙盒插件：3D 装配协作感知 + 项目级硬件在环仿真","id":"gh:1410431696","install_available":true,"language":"TypeScript","name":"dsh-breadboard","slug":"Noob-stupid/dsh-breadboard","topics":["agent-skills","breadboard","dsh-plugin","hardware","hardware-ai"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"DSH 嵌入式硬件沙盒插件：3D 装配协作感知 + 项目级硬件在环仿真"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"Web profile plugin — host half + browser half."},{"id":"p3s1","text":"> **English**: README.md | **中文**: README.zh.md"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"## What it is / what it solves"},{"id":"p5s1","text":"Normally the parts of a hardware project you can only *try on the real board* are the wiring
itself,"},{"id":"p5s2","text":" the sensor semantics at register level, and the failure handling. This plugin moves those
into a vi"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"rtual scene that actually runs:"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"- **3D assembly** — drop parts from the built-in model library (ESP32, Raspberry Pi 4B, BME280,
HC-S"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"R501 PIR, LED module, MPL3115A2, breadboard), wire them port by port, and get a live
SSOT (single so"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"urce of truth) assembly state with topology and electrical checks.
- **Project-level hardware-in-the"},{"id":"p6s4","text":"-loop** — a **real Python process** runs **your project's code**.
A Python shim intercepts its `smbu"},{"id":"p6s5","text":"s`/I2C access and answers from virtual devices, so the project

data coming from the virtual chip).
- **Net"},{"id":"p6s7","text":"worked-device emulation** (a second, separate class of virtual hardware) — a device that
actively PO"},{"id":"p6s8","text":"STs to **your** external HTTP backend on a real cadence: register → pull config →
periodic report. V"},{"id":"p6s9","text":"erified end-to-end against a real seat-selection system
(device → HTTP → backend state machine → dat"},{"id":"p6s10","text":"abase).
- **Failure injection** — unplug a wire, return NACK, force a reading, take a device offline"},{"id":"p6s11","text":", and
watch whether the project's error handling actually catches it.

switch the entire hardware setu"},{"id":"p6s13","text":" project folder to learn which hardware it needs, and
switch the entire hardware setup in one click."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"Requires DSH with the **`web`** profile and `webServer`, `tools` and `subprocess` services. The

plug"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"in does not activate at all, rather than activating with tools silently unregistered, a blank
panel,"},{"id":"p7s4","text":" or a simulation engine that cannot spawn."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## Reason codes and what to do about them"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"Failed assembly operations come back with a reason code (the contract's `WarningCode`, 12 of them,

| `direction_conflict` | two cu"},{"id":"p12s3","text":"rrent directions fight (output to output / two supplies tied together) | rearrange per current direc"},{"id":"p12s4","text":"tion: at least one end must become an input |

[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"## Known limitations"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"Honest list; none of these are hidden behind a default that pretends otherwise."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"- **This package is not published on npm.** Install from GitHub. A prebuilt tarball exists as a
rele"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"ase artifact, but there is no `npm install` line to offer.
- **The UI is Chinese only.** There is no"},{"id":"p19s3","text":" locale switch in the panel today, and no English UI
strings to promise.
- **Reading GPIO from the p"},{"id":"p19s4","text":"roject's Python code is not implemented.** `hw_set_occlusion` propagates
occlusion along the real wi"},{"id":"p19s5","text":"res into a networked device's readings, but the reverse direction —
project code calling `RPi.GPIO.i"},{"id":"p19s6","text":"nput()` through the shim — raises `NotImplementedError`, and the
bridge's `gpio_read` / `gpio_write`"},{"id":"p19s7","text":" are declared in the contract but not implemented
("protocol defined, behaviour model not implemente"},{"id":"p19s8","text":"d yet"). So a firmware that polls a pin and then
reports cannot be exercised end to end yet; a firmw"},{"id":"p19s9","text":"are that reports over HTTP can.
- **Networked devices are not rendered in the 3D scene yet.** They a"},{"id":"p19s10","text":"re in the SSOT
(`transport: 'network'`) and fully drivable by tools, but the front end does not draw"},{"id":"p19s11","text":" them.
- **Only measured / verified paths are claimed.** The networked-device chain was verified aga"},{"id":"p19s12","text":"inst a
real backend; an I2C-shaped *real* project has not been adapted yet — the I2C half is verifie"},{"id":"p19s13","text":"d by
this repository's own test projects.
- **Model size vs geometric fidelity is an open either/or*"},{"id":"p19s14","text":"* (documented in `docs/06` §6): scaling an
imported model to the declared real-board `size` slightly"},{"id":"p19s15","text":" deforms it. Today the plugin keeps real
board dimensions and aligns ports to the deformed pitch.
- "},{"id":"p19s16","text":"**`hw_set_occlusion` only reaches networked devices.** If the occluded part is wired to something
th"},{"id":"p19s17","text":"at is not a networked device with a `pinMap`, nothing propagates — and the tool says so in its
`reas"},{"id":"p19s18","text":"on` instead of silently succeeding.
- **The port count on some imported models is still converging**"},{"id":"p19s19","text":" (e.g. a handful of Raspberry Pi
header pins land on the PCB rather than on a pin mesh). Ports are u"},{"id":"p19s20","text":"sable; a few anchors are off by
fractions of a millimetre."}],"truncated":true}
